title: Qualcomm's CEO says AI firms want phones running 100-billion-parameter models by 2028
source_used: Startup Fortune (TokenPost read as a cross-check on dates)
key_facts: In an interview on 8 Oct, Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon said AI companies are asking for phones that can run 100-billion-parameter models continuously, all day, by 2028.
He declined to name the companies.

The newest Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and Elite Extreme Gen 6 chips are built on a 2nm process; the Extreme version can run mixture-of-experts models above 30 billion parameters on the device, so the target is more than three times that.
Amon described a shift to agentic AI, software that watches, reasons and acts for the user, which has to stay in memory and work in the background.
Amon has acknowledged a 'temporary constraint' on memory chip supply for smartphones and says it will push the industry toward more memory-efficient chip designs.
Fortune has reported that Amon is working with 'pretty much all' of the major AI players on undisclosed hardware projects.
Qualcomm has not said which companies are asking and there is no delivery commitment attached to the 2028 date; it is a target the industry is pushing toward, not a Qualcomm product launch.
quote_evidence: Cristiano Amon says the AI industry is already asking Qualcomm for phones that can run 100-billion-parameter models all day, every day, by 2028.
Qualcomm has not said which companies are asking for the capability.
Amon has been clear it's a target the industry is pushing toward, not a Qualcomm product launch.
why_it_matters_hint: AI labs reportedly want far larger AI models on phones, which would strain phone memory, battery and chip design.
event_date: Interview on 8 Oct 2026 (TokenPost says a first interview was on 23 Sep).
